sections.title: Molecular profile of cervical squamous cell carcinoma
sections.intro: Cervical SCC is **HPV-driven and APOBEC-mutagenic**, with frequent PI3K and 9p24.1 (PD-L1/PD-L2) alterations; **PD-L1 CPS ≥1 is the only treatment-selecting biomarker**. HPV-independent SCC is a minority with older age, p53 abnormality and worse survival [8]; TCGA splits SCC into keratin-high and keratin-low clusters [9].

cells: All histotypes (TCGA core set, n = 178): HPV-positive **169 (95%)**; alpha-9 types 120 (67%; HPV16 103); alpha-7 types 45 (25%; HPV18 27); HPV-negative **9 (5%)**. HPV integration in 141/169 (83%), including all HPV18 tumours. 7 of the 9 HPV-negative tumours fell in the endometrial-like group (8 tumours, 5 of them adenocarcinomas) [9]

49 true HPVI SCC among 89 HPV-negative SCC collected from 22 institutions (40 excluded as equivocal); median age 68 (36–88); 77.6% aged ≥60; uterine prolapse history 14.2%; p53-abnormal HPVI SCC the most aggressive [8]
PIK3CA mostly helical E542K/E545K; APOBEC signature enrichment in 150/192 exomes. HLA-A, HLA-B, NFE2L2, MAPK1, CASP8, SHKBP1 and TGFBR2 mutations were found **only in squamous tumours** [9]
Focal amplification 9p24.1 (CD274, PDCD1LG2) **21%**, 3q26.31 (TERC, MECOM) 78%, 3q28 (TP63) 77%, 17q12 (ERBB2) 17%, 7p11.2 (EGFR) 17%; the copy-number-high cluster was largely squamous [9]
4.04 mutations/Mb overall; 2.53 excluding 11 hypermutant tumours (>600 mutations) [9]

**SCC 91% (397/437)** vs usual-type adenocarcinoma 60% (35/58) in 647 profiled cervical carcinomas [10]. Trial screening (all histotypes): KEYNOTE-826 CPS ≥1 548/617, CPS ≥10 317 (51.4%), CPS <1 69 (11.2%) [2,11]; KEYNOTE-158 CPS ≥1 82/98 (83.7%), SCC 92/98 (93.9%) [12]

IHC 0 56.9%, 1+ 26.3%, 2+ 14.1%, **3+ 2.7%**; FISH amplification in all 3+ and 5.2% of 2+; reclassified HER2-positive 3.5%, HER2-low 39.6%; biopsy–hysterectomy discordance 48.3%, metastatic-site discordance 50.8% [13]
Membrane expression ≥1% in 93.3% of 404 assessed (innovaTV 301, all histotypes; not an eligibility criterion) [1]

MSI-H in **8/305 (2.6%)** of TCGA-CESC by MANTIS whole-exome analysis; MSI-H tumours were hypermutated (mean 5,675 vs 639 mutations, P = .003). CESC pools SCC and endocervical adenocarcinoma, so no SCC-specific rate is printed [14]. In 647 profiled cervical carcinomas MSI-H was 1.9% (12/647) overall and did not differ by PD-L1 status (2.2% vs 0%, P = 0.230; TMB-high 26.3% vs 17.2%, P = 0.058) [10]

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md:
- **PD-L1 22C3 CPS** on every recurrent/metastatic SCC before first line (pembrolizumab, T3A); ~9 in 10 are CPS ≥1 [10], so CPS <1 → check the sample.
- **HER2 IHC** at recurrence if T-DXd is considered (T3B); test the most recent sample [13].
- **HPV/p16 and p53** in older women: prognostic only [8].

sections.title: 1. Adjuvant therapy after radical hysterectomy (FIGO 2009 IA2–IIA)
sections.intro: Split by pathological risk: **1A intermediate risk** (node-negative, with combinations of deep stromal invasion, lymph–vascular space involvement and tumour size) and **1B high risk** (positive pelvic nodes, positive margins or parametrial involvement).

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT (46 Gy/23 fx to 50.4 Gy/28 fx) vs no further treatment
cols.pop: Stage IB, node-negative, ≥2 of: >1/3 stromal invasion, capillary lymphatic space involvement, clinical tumour diameter ≥4 cm
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 218/277 (78.7%); squamous recurrence 21/103 (20.4%) with RT vs 32/115 (27.8%) with observation, but **no SCC-specific HR is printed**; non-squamous 59 (34 RT, 25 observation). RT-by-histology interaction HR **0.23 (90% CI 0.07–0.74)**, P = 0.019 — larger benefit in adeno/adenosquamous (recurrence 8.8% vs 44.0%)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 adverse events 6% vs 2.1%; one death from grade 4 GI toxicity. HRs printed with 90% CIs

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT (median 50.4 Gy; conformal or IMRT) + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6 vs RT alone
cols.pop: Stage I–IIA (FIGO 2009), intermediate-risk combinations after radical hysterectomy and lymphadenectomy
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 233/316 (73.7%); **no histology subgroup is printed** — the RFS forest plot covers stage, risk factors, surgery and RT technique only
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 adverse events 43% vs 15% (P < 0.01); transient QoL decline with CRT, recovered by 36 weeks. RFS HR 0.47 (0.24–0.92) with conformal RT (subgroup, not for inference)

sections.title: 1B. High risk (node-positive, margin-positive or parametrial involvement)

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT 49.3 Gy/29 fx + cisplatin 70 mg/m² D1 + 5-FU 1000 mg/m²/day ×4 days, q3w ×4 (2 concurrent, 2 after RT) vs RT alone
cols.pop: Stage IA2, IB, IIA after radical hysterectomy with positive pelvic nodes, positive margins or parametrial involvement
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 97/127 (76%) vs 96/116 (83%). Non-squamous tumours did worse with RT alone (PFS, Fig 3), a difference that disappeared with chemotherapy; treatment-by-cell-type interaction P = .12 (PFS), .19 (OS); SCC-specific HR not reported
cols.hr: Printed RT vs CT + RT: PFS 2.01 (P = .003), OS 1.96 (P = .007); CI not printed
cols.tox: Grade 4 toxicity: 27 episodes in 21 CT + RT patients vs 4 on RT; ≥3 cycles in 71%. Median lesion size 2.1–2.2 cm

cols.regimen: *Same trial, retrospective univariate analysis*
cols.pop: *As above*
cols.hist: ***Included, not broken out***: *5-year survival with RT vs RT + CT — squamous 69% vs 80% (P = 0.019), non-squamous 55% vs 82% (P = 0.014); histology not prognostic within either arm (P = 0.170 / 0.764); no HRs or interaction test printed*
cols.pfs: *5-yr survival, RT vs RT + CT, by tumour size: ≤2 cm 77% vs 82%; >2 cm 58% vs 77%*
cols.os: *Overall 5-yr survival 66% vs 80% (median follow-up 5.2 yr). By nodes: 1 positive node 79% vs 83%; ≥2 nodes 55% vs 75%*
cols.tox: *Hypothesis-generating: smaller absolute benefit with 1 node or tumour ≤2 cm*

cols.regimen: Sequential chemoradiation (cisplatin 60–75 mg/m² + paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m² q21d, 2 cycles before and 2 after RT) vs concurrent weekly cisplatin 30–40 mg/m² + RT vs RT alone (45–50 Gy)
cols.pop: FIGO IB–IIA after radical hysterectomy with adverse pathological factors (intermediate and high risk mixed; nodal involvement lowest in RT arm, 18.3%); 8 Chinese hospitals
cols.hist: **SCC subgroup reported**: SCC 908/1048 (86.6%); recurrence HR SCRT vs RT **0.547 (0.357–0.839)**, CCRT vs RT 0.931 (0.635–1.365) — in SCC the concurrent weekly-cisplatin arm gave essentially no benefit over RT alone; in the AC/ASC group (n = 140) both SCRT (0.294) and CCRT (0.360) beat RT
cols.hr: DFS SCRT vs RT **0.52 (0.35–0.76)** (nodal-adjusted; unadjusted 0.61, 0.42–0.89); SCRT vs CCRT 0.65 (0.44–0.96); CCRT vs RT 0.79 (0.56–1.12), NS; cancer death SCRT vs RT 0.58 (0.35–0.95), SCRT vs CCRT 0.74 (0.45–1.23), CCRT vs RT 0.78 (0.49–1.23)
cols.tox: Concurrent weekly cisplatin did not improve DFS or cancer death over RT alone, in the trial overall or in SCC. Single-country trial mixing intermediate- and high-risk patients

cols.regimen: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC5 → pelvic RT 50.4 Gy vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²
cols.pop: Stage IB–IIB after surgery, high risk
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 197/263 (74.9%); histology was not a significant prognostic factor for PFS or OS, and no histology-by-treatment interaction was analysed
cols.os: 5-yr survival 85.8% vs 78.9%, P = 0.25 (abstract); 84.2% vs 77.4%, P = 0.34 in the Results text
cols.hr: Exploratory multivariate PFS 0.483 (0.25–0.92), P = 0.028; OS 0.59 (0.30–1.18), P = 0.137 — the authors call the model unreliable (26 disease events)
cols.tox: Early termination 12.9% vs 32.1% (P = 0.001); alopecia 87.9% vs 4.1%, neurotoxicity 65.9% vs 15.6%; more grade 3–4 haematological toxicity with CCRT

cols.regimen: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC6 q3w ×6 vs CCRT (50.4 Gy + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²)
cols.pop: Stage IB–IIB after radical hysterectomy with pelvic nodal metastasis and/or parametrial invasion
cols.hist: **Included**: SCC, adenocarcinoma and adenosquamous eligible
cols.tox: **Design-only row (ongoing trial, no results).** Non-inferiority margin OS HR 1.33, 118 per arm; minimisation includes SCC vs non-SCC, so an SCC subgroup is planned. No PubMed results publication found (2026-09-15)

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- Only STARS reports an SCC HR (SCRT vs RT recurrence 0.547; CCRT vs RT 0.931, NS) [23]; in GOG-92/109 the non-squamous minority drove or modified the effect [6,21,22].
- Intermediate risk: RT cuts recurrence without an OS gain [6]; adding weekly cisplatin (GOG-263) did not help and tripled toxicity [20].
- High risk: cisplatin/5-FU + RT is the only regimen with an OS benefit [21]; RTOG 0724 is unpublished (see Open items).
- Context: minimally invasive radical hysterectomy worse than open (LACC) [26]; simple hysterectomy non-inferior in low-risk disease (SHAPE) [27].

sections.title: 2. Primary treatment of locally advanced disease (FIGO 2008/2009 IB2–IVA; FIGO 2018 IB3–IVA)
2A. Definitive chemoradiation: backbone, schedule, induction and adjuvant chemotherapy

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w ×3 vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 93/104 (89.4%); no histology subgroup
cols.pfs: Recurrence 24.5% vs 29.4% (P = 0.510); PFS "almost identical" (data not shown)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 22.6% vs 39.2% (P = 0.03); compliance 92.5% vs 86.3%. Small trial; the phase III TACO trial (below) did not confirm superiority

cols.regimen: Induction weekly carboplatin AUC2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² ×6 → CCRT vs CCRT alone (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×5 + 45–50.4 Gy EBRT + brachytherapy, EQD2 78–86 Gy)
cols.pop: FIGO 2008 IB1 node-positive, IB2, IIA, IIB, IIIB, IVA (IIB 70%, IIIB 11%; nodes positive 43%)
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 411/500 (82%); randomization minimised on squamous vs non-squamous, but **no histology-subgroup HR is printed in the article** (appendix forest plots only; every subgroup CI included the overall HR)
cols.tox: Grade ≥3 adverse events 59% vs 48%; median 7 days from induction to CCRT; ≥5 induction cycles in 92%

cols.regimen: RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6 vs RT + cisplatin 50 mg/m² D1, D29 + 5-FU 4 g/m² 96-h + hydroxyurea (CFH) vs RT + hydroxyurea 3 g/m² twice weekly
cols.pop: Stage IIB, III, IVA with surgically negative para-aortic nodes
cols.os: Deaths 34% vs 33% vs 50%; 10-yr OS **53% vs 53% vs 34%** (2007); median follow-up of survivors 106 mo
cols.hr: vs hydroxyurea — cisplatin: PFS 0.57 (0.42–0.78), OS **0.61 (0.44–0.85)**; CFH: PFS 0.55 (0.40–0.75), OS 0.58 (0.41–0.81). Long-term progression/death relative risk 0.57 (0.43–0.75) and 0.51 (0.38–0.67)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 leukopenia ~23% (cisplatin) vs ~46% (CFH); no treatment-related deaths. Delayed radiation toxicity 1.7% (cisplatin) vs 1.2% (hydroxyurea), P = .680 (2007). Established weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²

cols.regimen: RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² (max 70 mg/wk) ×6 → extrafascial hysterectomy vs RT → hysterectomy
cols.pop: Bulky (≥4 cm) stage IB, radiographically node-negative
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 152/186 (82%) vs 147/183 (80%)
cols.pfs: Recurrence 21% vs 37%; 72-mo alive and disease-free (adjusted) 71% vs 60%
cols.hr: Progression 0.51 (0.34–0.75), death 0.54 (0.34–0.86) (printed as relative risks, 1999); at 101 mo: progression relative risk 0.61 (0.43–0.85), adjusted death HR **0.63 (0.43–0.91)**
cols.tox: Any grade 3–4 AE 35% vs 13%; no excess late effects. Adjuvant hysterectomy since discontinued

cols.regimen: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + gemcitabine 125 mg/m² ×6 with EBRT 50.4 Gy → brachytherapy → cisplatin 50 mg/m² D1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² D1, 8 ×2 vs weekly cisplatin CCRT → brachytherapy
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, KPS ≥70
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: "non-adenocarcinoma" (squamous, poorly differentiated and adenosquamous pooled) 483/515 (93.8%); pure SCC fraction not printed and no histology subgroup reported
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 toxicity 86.5% vs 46.3% (P < .001); two deaths possibly treatment-related (experimental arm). Two changes at once (gemcitabine concurrent + adjuvant)

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT 45 Gy + cisplatin 75 mg/m² + 5-FU 4 g/m² 96-h ×3 vs extended-field (pelvic + para-aortic) RT alone
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, or IB–IIA with tumour ≥5 cm or positive pelvic nodes; para-aortic nodes negative
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 176 (90%) vs 174 (90%)
cols.hr: Printed as relative risks (2004): OS **0.48 (0.35–0.67)**, DFS 0.49 (0.36–0.66), locoregional failure 0.42 (0.28–0.64), distant metastasis 0.48 (0.32–0.73); 51% reduction in death or recurrence (95% CI 34%–64%)
cols.tox: Acute grade 3–4 in the chemotherapy arm: 33% grade 3, 11% grade 4, 1% grade 5; late toxicity similar. Stage III–IVA 5-yr OS 59% (46–72) vs 45% (32–59), RR 0.63 (0.39–1.04), P = .07 (2004; 116 patients, not powered)

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin + 5-FU infusion vs RT + oral hydroxyurea
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, negative para-aortic nodes and cytologic washings
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 335/368 (156, 88.1% vs 179, 93.7%); no histology-specific subgroup HR printed
cols.os: Deaths 79 (45%) vs 108 (57%); median not reached vs 59.8 mo, P = .018
cols.hr: Printed as relative risks with 90% CIs: death **0.74 (0.58–0.95)**, P = .018; progression or death 0.79 (0.62–0.99), P = .033
cols.tox: Severe or life-threatening leukopenia 4% vs 24%. Cell type was the most imbalanced baseline factor (non-squamous 12% vs 6%)

cols.regimen: Radical RT (EBRT + brachytherapy) + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² vs same RT
cols.pop: Stage IB–IVA with central disease ≥5 cm or histologically positive pelvic nodes
cols.hist: **SCC-only trial**
cols.hr: Printed RT alone vs CRT: OS **1.13 (0.77–1.67)** in the Results text (abstract prints 1.10, 0.75–1.62), P = .42; NS
cols.tox: Negative in SCC; authors stress radiotherapy quality (median RT 49–51 days) and note a 46% chance of missing a true 10-point 5-yr OS gain

cols.regimen: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×5 CCRT → carboplatin AUC5 + paclitaxel 155 mg/m² q21d ×4 vs CCRT alone
cols.pop: FIGO 2008 IB1 node-positive, IB2, II, IIIB, IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 358 (79%) CCRT vs 383 (83%) adjuvant; squamous or adenosquamous 377 vs 395 (post hoc): OS HR **0.90 (0.68–1.20)**, P interaction 0.98; PFS HR 0.86 (0.68–1.10), P interaction 0.94 — no differential effect by histology
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 20% vs 8%, anaemia 18% vs 8%; 22% never started adjuvant chemotherapy

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w ×3 vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 114 (81.4%) triweekly vs 137 (90.1%) weekly (251/292, 86.0%); no histology subgroup
cols.tox: Fewer grade 3–4 haematological toxicities (P < 0.001), fewer chemotherapy delays and better QoL with triweekly

cols.regimen: *Weekly carboplatin 100 mg/m² + RT (prospective) vs historical weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + RT*
cols.pop: *Locally advanced, patients with morbidity risks / poor general condition*
cols.hist: ***Included, not broken out***: *SCC ~91%; no histology subgroup*
cols.tox: *Overall response 90.0% vs 87.5% (P = 0.31). Grade 3–4 toxicity similar (more thrombocytopenia with carboplatin); 7.5 vs 6.0 cycles received. The only carboplatin-substitution comparison retrieved*

rows.name: GOG chemoradiation trials pooled by histology

cols.regimen: *Cisplatin-based CRT vs RT without cisplatin (GOG 85, 120, 123, 165, 191)*
cols.pop: *Stage IB2–IVA*
cols.hist: ***SCC reference group, retrospective***: adeno/adenosquamous vs SCC adjusted PFS 1.21 (0.98–1.51), OS 1.25 (1.00–1.56). With cisplatin CRT: similar PFS (P = 0.315) and OS (HR 1.12, P = 0.459), 112 vs 842; without concurrent cisplatin: worse OS (HR 1.39, P = 0.0499), 70 vs 647; within-stratum CIs not printed
cols.tox: *Adverse effects similar across histologies; pulmonary toxicity 1.1% SCC vs 3.3% non-squamous*

notes.title: Traps in Table 2A
notes.md:
- **Cisplatin CCRT benefit is not uniform:** the SCC-only NCIC trial was negative [37], the GOG/RTOG trials positive [4,31,34,36]; meta-analysis HR 0.81 (6% absolute 5-yr gain) [41].
- RTOG 90-01 changed two variables; GOG-120 and GOG-85 used hydroxyurea controls [4,34,36].
- **Adjuvant chemo after CCRT is negative** (OUTBACK) [38]; **short induction before CCRT is positive** (INTERLACE) [29].
- Triweekly vs weekly cisplatin: no difference in TACO [39]; carboplatin substitution has no randomized support [40].

cols.regimen: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w ×5 with cisplatin CCRT (EBRT + brachytherapy) → pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w ×15 vs placebo
cols.pop: Newly diagnosed high-risk: FIGO 2014 IB2–IIB node-positive or III–IVA any node status; PD-L1 not required
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 884/1060 (83.4%) at the PFS analysis and 885/1060 (83.5%) at the OS analysis; **histology is not a protocol-specified subgroup in either paper, so no SCC HR exists**
cols.os: 36-mo OS **82.6% vs 74.8%** (second interim; median follow-up 29.9 mo)
cols.tox: Grade ≥3 adverse events 78% vs 70%; potentially immune-mediated 39% vs 17%. Cisplatin only. PFS benefit concentrated in FIGO 2014 III–IVA (HR 0.58, 0.42–0.80) vs node-positive IB2–IIB (0.91, 0.63–1.31) [42]; disease-specific survival HR 0.64 (0.46–0.89) [43]

cols.regimen: Durvalumab 1500 mg q4w with and after CCRT (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC2 ×5 + 45 Gy + image-guided brachytherapy), up to 24 cycles vs placebo
cols.pop: FIGO 2009 IB2–IIB node-positive, or ≥III any node status
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 642/770 (83%); histology was not a prespecified subgroup — no SCC HR is printed
cols.pfs: Median not reached either arm; 12-mo PFS 76.0% vs 73.3%
cols.hr: PFS **0.84 (0.65–1.08)**, P = 0.17; NS. OS 0.78 (0.55–1.10) — not formally interpretable because the hierarchical testing procedure was not met
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 anaemia 20% vs 15%; treatment-related deaths 5 vs 1. Authors suggest exploring high PD-L1 expression

cols.regimen: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6 CCRT → ipilimumab 3 or 10 mg/kg q21d ×4
cols.pop: FIGO IB2–IVA with positive pelvic and/or para-aortic nodes
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 28/32 (88%); no histology subgroup
cols.tox: Grade 3 toxicity 2/21 (9.5%); MTD 10 mg/kg; HPV genotype not associated with PFS or OS

notes.title: Reading Table 2B
notes.md: KEYNOTE-A18 is the only positive immuno-chemoradiation trial (OS HR 0.67) [43]; CALLA was negative [44]. **Neither reports an SCC result** (83% squamous in both). KEYNOTE-A18 used cisplatin only and excluded node-negative IB2–IIB [43].

notes.title: Trial dosing vs NTUH templates (Table 2)
notes.md:
- Weekly cisplatin CCRT and induction templates match GOG-120/123 and INTERLACE [4,29,31].
- ⚠️ CC CCRT (Cisplatin+Keytruda) for豪哥的VIP: 2 pembrolizumab cycles, no maintenance; KEYNOTE-A18 gave 200 mg q3w ×5 then 400 mg q6w ×15 [42].
- ⚠️ CC CCRT (Carboplatin+Keytruda) for豪哥的VIP: no trial support (KEYNOTE-A18 cisplatin only [43]; carboplatin allowed in CALLA, negative [44]).
- CC PF(Cisplatin and 5FU(2600)) and the two P-HDFL templates match no trial dose [21,34].

sections.title: 3. Recurrent or metastatic disease
sections.intro: Split by line: **3A** first line (radiosensitising cisplatin allowed) · **3B** after platinum ± bevacizumab ± PD-(L)1 inhibitor. Every row carries a `Prior systemic therapy` column.

notes.title: Why this split exists
notes.md: 3A trials mixed IVB, persistent and recurrent disease, mostly after radiosensitising cisplatin only. Prior cisplatin lowers response and survival [45,46,47], so 3A medians are not second-line expectations.

sections.title: 3A. First-line systemic therapy for recurrent, persistent or metastatic disease

rows.name: KEYNOTE-826
rows.cite: Colombo 2021; final OS Monk 2023; 5-yr Hasegawa 2026; subgroups Tewari 2024

notes.title: Reading notes for Table 3
notes.md:
- **3A:** KEYNOTE-826, COMPASSION-16 and BEATcc all have SCC OS HRs close to their trial-wide HRs [7,49,50]; they were not compared directly.
- **3A backbone:** cisplatin–paclitaxel is the reference [55]; carboplatin–paclitaxel is non-inferior overall but inferior without prior cisplatin [47].
- **3B:** cemiplimab and tisotumab vedotin OS benefits hold in SCC [1,3]; evidence after first-line pembrolizumab is limited to the innovaTV 301 subgroup. Single-arm ORRs are not comparable with randomized medians.
- Old single agents (ORR 8–21%) set the pre-immunotherapy salvage baseline [61,62,64,65,66].

notes.title: Reading Table 4
notes.md:
- NACT → surgery has not beaten chemoradiation: worse DFS (Gupta, SCC-only) and worse PFS (EORTC 55994) [70,71]; almost half of EORTC surgical patients still needed RT.
- NACT did not beat surgery alone (JCOG 0102) [69]; the 2004 meta-analysis's RT-alone control is no longer standard [73].
- Induction before CCRT (INTERLACE) is the one positive neoadjuvant strategy [29]. JGOG1082 and CSEM 006 are design-only [25,72]; no fertility-sparing RCTs.
